title: Arsenal vs. Borussia Dortmund: Preview, Predictions, Talking Points
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack8:30 PM ESTArsenal and Borussia Dortmund meet for the first time since 2014. / Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty Images (Arsenal), Kristian Skeie/UEFA/Getty Images (Borussia Dortmund)Arsenal and Borussia Dortmund face off for the first time in 12 years in the Champions League on Tuesday evening, with the Gunners playing host to this Matchday 5 league phase encounter.

Emiliano Martínez started between the posts for Arsenal, and Yaya Sanogo scored within two minutes when these two teams last met in 2014, with future Gunners Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang and Henrikh Mkhitaryan starting for the visiting Germans.

The pair collide in good shape. Arsenal dropped points at Newcastle United on Saturday, yet still have a healthy buffer at the Premier League’s summit, while Dortmund moved to the top of the Bundesliga table after beating Borussia Mönchengladbach 1–0 in the wake of Bayern Munich’s 1–1 draw with FC Köln.

Just a point, but nine places separate these two teams in the league phase table. Each has a single blemish on their records, with Arsenal drawing 2–2 at Bayern on Matchday 3 and Dortmund losing 1–0 to Bodø/Glimt on Matchday 2.
The Gunners claimed a 2–1 victory at Slavia Prague last time out, while Tuesday’s visitors defeated Real Betis by the same scoreline at Signal Iduna Park.

Arsenal have been inevitable at this stage of the competition under Arteta. / Shaun Brooks/CameraSport/Getty ImagesArsenal have an outstanding record at this stage of the competition under Mikel Arteta, and although Borussia Dortmund enter this match as the Bundesliga leaders, the hosts are still big favorites to continue their league phase dominance.

A top-eight berth isn’t to be scoffed at, and given the two fixtures that are heading Arsenal’s way—Real Madrid (H) and Real Betis (A)—before they host Sabah on Matchday 8, it’s imperative that they win on Tuesday.

Dortmund are plucky operators under Niko Kovač and have rediscovered themselves after dealing with an identity crisis when predecessor Nuri Șahin was at the helm. However, they have yet to prove that they can go to places like Emirates Stadium and claim a huge victory.

Dortmund’s manager has a bad record in England. / Sebastian El-Saqqa/firo sportphoto/Getty Images• Arsenal’s imperious European form: The Gunners are aiming to match their longest unbeaten record in the group stage/league phase of this competition, which stands at 17. Mikel Arteta‘s side have won 15 of their previous 16 matches, drawing the other (2–2 vs. Bayern Munich). Arsenal have also triumphed in their last 12 league phase home games.

• Niko Kovač’s sticky record in England: The Dortmund manager has a poor record against English opposition, with his only victory in five meetings with Premier League teams arriving when he was in charge of Bayern Munich, who infamously thrashed Tottenham Hotspur 7–2 in 2019.

• Defense comes to the fore: Game state is imperative for this Arsenal team, and they’re ever so tough to beat after scoring the first goal, thanks to their stout defense. The Gunners have scored first in each of their last 12 league phase home matches, which is a major reason why their record at this stage of the competition is so impressive. They’ve conceded just three goals so far in Europe this season.
